# Omit the RSA Private-Key Screenshot

**Decision.** Do not use the natural illustration for the applied-cryptography lab, because that page
prints a private key. Use the signature-verification page instead, and say in the repository that the
substitution was made and why.

**Date.** 2026-07-25 (the publishing commit), `assets/` of
[[cybersecurity-engineering-laboratories]].

## Why

The lab's most representative page is the terminal where the keypair is generated — it is the step the
whole lab is built on, and it is the obvious thing to show. It also prints the key in full:

> "The obvious illustration for lab 7 is not used. The natural screenshot for that lab is the terminal
> where the RSA keypair is generated — and it prints the full 2048-bit private key. The
> signature-verification page is used instead."
> — Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories/README.md, 2026-07-25

The reasoning generalises past this one key. The keypair was a throwaway generated for a lab exercise,
so on a narrow reading nothing is at risk. The rule applied is stronger and is stated separately for
the PKCS#12 case:

> "No private key files are committed. ... a `.p12` is a private key container by definition and those
> do not belong in a public repository regardless of what is inside them."
> — Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories/README.md, 2026-07-25

**"Regardless of what is inside them"** is the decision. Classify by *kind*, not by assessed value. A
rule that requires judging each key's importance fails the first time the judgement is wrong or
hurried, and secret-scanning tools and human readers both key off the shape of the thing, not its
provenance.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Publish it — the key is throwaway** | requires the reader to trust a per-item risk assessment; normalises private keys appearing in repositories |
| **Redact the key region of the screenshot** | partial redaction of a dense block reliably misses something, and a cropped terminal is not obviously complete |
| **Regenerate with a tiny key for the screenshot** | still a private key in the image, and now a misleading one |
| **Omit lab 7 from the illustrations entirely** | loses the lab that best represents the defensive half of the course |

**TODO:** only the outcome is evidenced. The repository states which page was used instead and why;
it does not record these four options being weighed. They are stated here as the alternatives, not as
the author's deliberation.

## What makes it a decision rather than a preference

It cost something specific — the second-best illustration for the lab — and it is recorded at the
point of use. `assets/README.md` names the source page of every screenshot *and* names the omission:

> "Lab 7's key-generation page is deliberately not among these: it prints a full RSA-2048 private key
> to the terminal."
> — Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories/assets/README.md, 2026-07-25

An omission that is not documented is indistinguishable from an oversight. Writing it down is what
converts "there is no keygen screenshot" into evidence of a rule being followed. Compare
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

Structurally the same defaulting appears in `.gitignore`, which excludes `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.pem`,
`*.key`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore` and `id_rsa*` so the rule holds without anyone remembering it —
[[secrets-from-environment-only]] is the same instinct applied to configuration. See [[openssl]] for
why key-generation output looks the way it does, and [[public-key-infrastructure]] for why the private
half must never leave the machine that made it.

**This page deliberately does not describe what the omitted screenshot contained beyond the fact that
it was a private key.** Reproducing the omission would defeat it.
